content: 1. A controlled trial was conducted to compare the efficacy of insulin Lispro with human soluble insulin in patients with type 1 diabetes undergoing intensified insulin therapy. This study was performed by the UK Trial Group and published in Diabetic Medicine in 2000. 2. Tamás G and colleagues conducted a randomized multinational study to evaluate glycemic control in type 1 diabetic patients using optimized insulin Aspart or human insulin. The findings were published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice in 2001. 3. Bott U and colleagues investigated the impact of the rapid-acting insulin analogue, insulin Aspart, on quality of life and treatment satisfaction in patients with type 1 diabetes. The results were published in Diabetic Medicine in 2003. 4. DeVries JH and the Tri-Continental Insulin Aspart Study Group performed a randomized trial comparing insulin Aspart with intensified basal NPH insulin supplementation in individuals with type 1 diabetes. The study was published in Diabetic Medicine in 2003. 5. Kotsanos JG and colleagues assessed health-related quality-of-life outcomes from multinational clinical trials of insulin Lispro, focusing on the benefits of this new diabetes therapy. The results were published in Diabetes Care in 1997. 6. Home PD and the European Insulin Aspart Study Group conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing insulin Aspart with human insulin for long-term blood glucose control in type 1 diabetes mellitus. The findings were published in Diabetic Medicine in 2000. 7. Renner R and the German Humalog-CSII Study Group evaluated the use of insulin Lispro in continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion therapy through a multicenter trial. The results were published in Diabetes Care in 1999. 8. Manini R and colleagues demonstrated that insulin Glargine improves glycemic control and health-related quality of life in patients with type 1 diabetes. The study was published in Nutrition, Metabolism and Cardiovascular Diseases in 2007. 9. Chatterjee S and colleagues conducted the GLASS study, a randomized cross-over trial comparing the efficacy of Glargine versus NPH insulin in combination with insulin Aspart in a basal-bolus regimen for type 1 diabetes. The findings were published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice in 2007. 10. Witthaus E and colleagues compared treatment satisfaction and psychological well-being between insulin Glargine and NPH insulin in patients with type 1 diabetes. The study was published in Diabetic Medicine in 2001. 11. Ashwell SG and colleagues evaluated treatment satisfaction and quality of life in individuals with type 1 diabetes using insulin Glargine plus insulin Lispro versus NPH insulin plus unmodified human insulin. The findings were published in Diabetes Care in 2008. 12. Machado-Alba JE and colleagues assessed the quality of life in patients with diabetes mellitus treated with either conventional or analogue insulins. The study was published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice in 2016. 13. McNally PG and colleagues used continuous glucose monitoring to measure the frequency of low glucose values in individuals with type 2 diabetes using biphasic insulin Aspart 30 compared with biphasic human insulin 30. This double-blind crossover study was published in Diabetes Care in 2007. 14. Clements MR and colleagues demonstrated improved glycemic control with thrice-daily biphasic insulin Aspart compared to twice-daily biphasic human insulin in patients with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. The study was published in Diabetes, Obesity and Metabolism in 2008. 15. Bradley C reviewed alternative designs to conventional randomized controlled trials for medical and educational intervention studies. The review was published in Diabetes Care in 1993. 16. Baker E and colleagues investigated the relationship between the interval of insulin injection and meal timing with glycated hemoglobin levels. The study was published in Practical Diabetes International in 2001. 17. A summary of findings on long-acting insulin analogues indicated that the quality of evidence for critical outcomes such as HbA1c, all-cause mortality, and severe hypoglycemia was often downgraded due to imprecision, inconsistency, and indirectness. These findings were adapted from multiple studies, including Cochrane reviews. 18. Short-acting insulin analogues were evaluated against regular human insulin for adults with type 1 diabetes. The evidence for outcomes such as mortality, health-related quality of life, and progression of nephropathy was limited or insufficiently reported, as noted in a Cochrane review.
